title: Shut down the company
summary: Wind down and dissolve the corporation: board and stockholder dissolution consents, the final payroll and contractor terminations, vendor cancellations, final tax returns with IRS account closure, the Delaware certificate of dissolution with franchise-tax true-up, state withdrawals, bank closure with final distributions, and records retention.

parts.title: Draft board and stockholder dissolution consents
parts.guidance: Prepare the dissolution approvals with counsel using ownership, liabilities, assets and the proposed closure route. Address employees, creditors, contracts, taxes and records in the plan. Identify filings triggered by adoption, including Form 966 where applicable, and calendar them before signatures. Resolve the company’s eligibility for the proposed route and the decision-makers required to authorize it.

parts.title: Sign the dissolution consents
parts.guidance: Obtain the approvals required for the chosen dissolution route from the actual directors, stockholders or other decision-makers. Present the final plan and financial consequences, then check voting requirements, capacities and document consistency. Record the true adoption date and notify the closure coordinator, because filings may run from that event. Resolve incomplete approvals before relying on the plan as authorized.

parts.title: Run the final payroll and terminate contractors
parts.guidance: Resolve final compensation, notices, benefits, contractor invoices, equipment and access for each departing person and location. HR, payroll and counsel handle the relevant local requirements. The responsible company representatives authorize termination communications and payments. Reconcile completed payments and outstanding claims, and retain the staff access needed to finish payroll reporting, tax work and closure.

parts.title: Cancel vendor contracts and subscriptions
parts.guidance: Review contracts and subscriptions for termination rights, notice methods, final charges and data exports. Include services holding records needed after closure. Send authorized cancellation notices, retain acknowledgements and verify billing stops. Export necessary records before accounts disappear, and keep essential communications and storage running until their custodians can complete dependent closure work.

parts.title: File the certificate of dissolution and franchise-tax true-up
parts.guidance: Use the reviewed dissolution route for this entity. For a Delaware corporation, reconcile the certificate with its corporate approvals and the state’s annual-report and franchise-tax requirements. The authorized officer approves the filing, effective timing and payments. Track acceptance and continue winding up. A foreign option requires its local procedure and a fresh plan for the subsequent tax, creditor and distribution work.

options.title: Default — Delaware dissolution forms
options.summary: Select the appropriate Delaware dissolution certificate and confirm the corporate approvals supporting it. Reconcile annual-report and franchise-tax requirements for the corporation ending its existence. The authorized officer approves the certificate, timing and payments before submission. Keep the accepted filing and continue the separate work on claims, taxes, distributions and records.

verify.how: The Delaware entity search shows the corporation's status as dissolved once the certificate is stamped.

cost.note: Certificate of Dissolution (§275) filing fee; franchise taxes must be brought current to dissolve, and the §391 short form is $50 where eligible.

options.title: India - STK-2 strike-off or IBC liquidation
options.summary: Review the Indian company’s activity, liabilities, assets and filing status with a local professional to determine the available closure route. Assess strike-off or formal liquidation against current requirements before choosing either. Establish the necessary approvals, creditor treatment and tax work, then carry out authorized filings through the local process. The subsequent US forms do not constitute an Indian closure procedure.

options.title: UK - DS01 voluntary strike-off
options.summary: Check voluntary strike-off eligibility against the company’s trading, creditor, asset and insolvency position. Resolve required communications and remaining assets and obligations before the authorized directors approve applying. Follow Companies House notices through the actual outcome. If the company is ineligible, assess the appropriate alternative closure route.
options.when: Winding up in the United Kingdom

options.title: Germany - liquidation + Sperrjahr
options.summary: Confirm the German dissolution decision, liquidators, registry filings and creditor process with local counsel. Assess assets and liabilities and the distribution restrictions in GmbHG section 73 before authorizing payouts. Track liquidation separately from final register removal, keeping the required corporate and registry evidence. Use the local sequence and applicable German tax filings for subsequent closure work.

options.title: France - dissolution then radiation
options.summary: Assess whether voluntary dissolution fits the French company’s financial and ownership facts. Follow the appropriate dissolution decision, liquidator’s work, closure accounts and radiation process, with associated tax and social filings identified separately. Obtain the required approvals for submissions and distributions and retain decisions and registry evidence. The local closure sequence governs follow-up, including which tax forms apply.

parts.title: Wait for the dissolution to be accepted
parts.guidance: Follow the registry’s acceptance or correction requests and verify the effective dissolution date against the filing. Resolve discrepancies with the filer or counsel and save the accepted record. Continue the applicable tax, creditor and records work under the closure plan. Registry acceptance is one milestone within winding up; it does not establish that remaining obligations are finished.

parts.title: CPA prepares the final federal and state returns
parts.guidance: Give the CPA the final books, asset dispositions, payroll, contractor payments, prior returns and closure approvals. Identify the returns, periods, final-return designations and related forms for this entity, with each deadline tracked independently. Resolve open accounting items before return review. For a foreign entity option, establish the relevant local tax work before applying US forms.

parts.title: Sign the final return jurats and Form 966
parts.guidance: Review final returns and any required Form 966 against the closure records, then obtain the proper human signature or electronic authorization. Check Form 966’s separate deadline from adoption of the dissolution or liquidation plan; it may precede final-return preparation. Keep required resolution attachments with the filing and resolve factual discrepancies before submission.

parts.title: File the final returns and close the IRS account
parts.guidance: Authorize the reviewed final tax filings and check acknowledgements and payments. Reconcile outstanding federal obligations before requesting closure of the IRS business account under current instructions. Keep the EIN in historical records as the entity’s permanent identifier. Assign a reachable person to later notices, and track actual account-closure status separately from the company’s dissolution filing.

verify.how: The final returns are marked final and the IRS closing-a-business checklist is completed for the EIN account.

parts.title: Withdraw foreign-state registrations
parts.guidance: Check every foreign-state registration for its withdrawal procedure and outstanding reports, taxes or clearances. Submit the approved withdrawal and fee, then follow it through acceptance. Keep agent coverage where still required during closure and update the jurisdiction record when withdrawal is confirmed. A home-state dissolution does not automatically terminate registrations elsewhere.

verify.how: Each state's business search shows the registration withdrawn or terminated.

parts.title: Close bank accounts and distribute remaining assets
parts.guidance: Reconcile cash with remaining debts, taxes, fees and contingent claims. Counsel and the financial adviser determine appropriate reserves and distributions under the winding-up plan. Authorized company representatives approve transfers to verified recipients. Close accounts only after remaining payment and receipt needs are resolved, and preserve the final statements and distribution evidence for the custodian.

parts.title: Archive corporate records for retention
parts.guidance: Preserve corporate decisions, ownership, contracts, employment, tax and financial records with the closure evidence. Apply the relevant retention requirements and legal holds. Name a reachable custodian and test access to storage that will survive closed subscriptions and employee accounts. Arrange where future notices will arrive and who can retrieve documents or address unresolved matters.

metadata.supportReason: The agent drafts the consents, runs the final payroll, cancels vendors, and prepares every filing; the dissolution consents and return jurats need real signatures, and the Delaware, IRS, and bank-closure steps are portal or mail work.

geoNotes.summary: Two exits: MCA strike-off via form STK-2 for a company with no liabilities, or a formal voluntary liquidation under the IBC run by an insolvency professional and overseen by the IBBI — both slower and more document-heavy than a US dissolution.

A solvent company applies for voluntary strike-off with a £33 DS01 filing to Companies House (or a members' voluntary liquidation for larger balance sheets) — closer to one filing than the DE dissolution + IRS final-return chain.

Winding up a GmbH is slow by design: a notarized dissolution resolution, liquidators registered, creditors publicly invited — then a mandatory one-year Sperrjahr before assets can distribute and the company is finally deleted from the Handelsregister.

The sequence is dissolution (shareholder decision + legal-announcement publication), a liquidation phase closing the accounts, then radiation from the RCS — every step filed through the guichet unique.

Wind-down runs through the registry's dissolution-and-liquidation channel (the encerrar-o-negócio guide maps it), plus the final Modelo 22 and IES and the cessação de atividade declarations to the tax authority and Segurança Social.

A solvent corporation dissolves by shareholder-authorized articles of dissolution filed with Corporations Canada — close the CRA program accounts (payroll, GST/HST) and file the final T2 before the certificate issues.
